_about: Hand-drawn lake polygons ABSENT from the FWA waterbody layer, ingested as real lake nodes. See pipeline/hack/added_lakes/README.md for the wbk minting scheme and the one thing that makes a lake a lake: the fids inside the polygon are re-stamped with its wbk, which is what breaks the stream run and mints the lake:{wbk} boundary.

properties.name: Redsand Lake
properties.note: DFO Region 6 scope B(ii) regulates 'Redsand Lake' including tributaries (coho 4/day only 1 over 50 cm Sep 1-Oct 31; no fishing for chinook all year). FWA has no polygon for it, so no water of that name exists at all — an exact lookup for 'Redsand Lake' returns nothing. Treston Lake, 441 m south, carries the name variant 'TRESTON LAKE  REDSAND LAKE' from a BATHYMETRY map label (source: bathymetry in name_variants.json) — a sheet covering both lakes, which is itself evidence they are two waters. It indexes only under its own full string, so Treston never answered to 'Redsand Lake'; a substring search suggests otherwise and is not how the matcher works. Sits on the Kitsumkalum River (blk 360883243, wsc 400-195432) in the section 'between Treston Lake and Kitsumkalum Lake' — the same river Treston sits on, 441 m north of it. Hand-drawn, supplied by the curator 2026-09-01, EPSG:3857 -> 4326. 40.49 ha, 25 vertices, centre 54.70592/-128.77963, MU 6-15. Derived ids: id 1 -> wbk -1, gnis -9000001 — both NEGATIVE, and the gnis is beyond the real range in magnitude (real gnis run 1,642..8,000,027) so it cannot be confused with a real id even if a sign is lost.

claims.note: unnamed tributary, ~228 m inside — the lake swallows its mouth

properties.name: Marsh Pond
properties.note: Region 2 MU 2-4 override 'MARSH POND' had no FWA polygon at all — the curation carried only a KML point in Aldergrove Regional Park (-122.45323, 49.00879), which the live matcher never reads (`override_typed_ids` resolves gnis/wbk/wsc/blk only), so the row pinned NOTHING. Polygon supplied by the curator from OpenStreetMap relation 2531058 v2 (changeset 94668116, natural=water, water=pond) — a multipolygon: 54-vertex outer ring (way 88807629) with one 27-vertex island (way 187905368, role inner) kept as a hole. 1.39 ha, centre 49.00899/-122.45317, EPSG:4326. The curated KML point falls INSIDE it. Isolated water: no stream fid overlaps it (nearest piece is Pepin Creek, blk 356286496, 348 m away), so it claims nothing and splits nothing — `mint_waterbody_nodes` gives it an edgeless lake node and `add_mu_sets` reads MU 2-4 off the polygon (Pepin Creek, the only water near it, is 2-4). Derived ids: id 2 -> wbk -2, gnis -9000002.

properties.name: Children's Fishing Pond
properties.note: The ungazetted 'Mission Creek Regional Park Children's Fishing Pond' that the Region 8 MU 8-10 override 'HALL ROAD (Mission) POND' names ALONGSIDE FWA waterbody 329460964 — two distinct ponds 194 m apart in the same park, both inside the regulated area. Only the FWA one had geometry; this one was a bare point (-119.42958, 49.87084). Polygon supplied by the curator from OpenStreetMap way 302989664 v1 (name='Children's Fishing Pond', natural=water, water=pond): 11 vertices, 0.22 ha, centre 49.87084/-119.42959, EPSG:4326. The curated point falls INSIDE it. Kept under its OWN name, NOT 'Hall Road Pond': 329460964 already carries the curated name 'HALL ROAD POND' (name_variants, source 'regulation') and is the only item that normalises to 'hall road pond' in MU 8-10 — a second one would make that lookup ambiguous and the matcher would drop it to UNMATCHED. The override pins BOTH wbks instead, and an override always beats name matching. Isolated water: no stream fid overlaps it (nearest piece is Mission Creek, blk 356569550, 539 m away), so it claims nothing and splits nothing. Derived ids: id 3 -> wbk -3, gnis -9000003.
